name: Dutch (Brujah Clan Leader of New Orleans)

system.concept: Idealist Brujah who came to New Orleans chasing a second Carthage
system.title: Clan Leader (Brujah)
system.biography:
Background

Dutch, an Idealist @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} from California, arrived in New Orleans in 1951 hoping to build a second Carthage alongside then-Prince Doran. He instead found the local @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} rabble-rousing with no higher purpose, confronted and displaced the clan's previous leader, and drove off or destroyed those who would not follow him. Realizing the city was built to serve the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} rather than any Brujah utopia, Dutch briefly considered contesting the princeship after Doran's 1955 assassination but backed down rather than lose his grip on the clan. He now heads the Underground Society, ostensibly to help refugee Kindred find their footing in the city but really to build a base of loyal newcomers he can call on later. He is the lone dissenting voice on the Prince's Council, and quietly protects Marcel's neglected childe Christopher, whom Dutch hopes to eventually steer toward the throne.

Roleplaying Hints

Calm, deliberate, and unusually rational for a Brujah — you see your ambitions as restoring what belongs to your clan, not as revolution for its own sake.

Disciplines (as printed, dot-rating, converted to owned Discipline Items on this Actor at Storyteller discretion): Celerity 4, Dominate 2, Fortitude 1, Obfuscate 2, Potence 3, Presence 3, Protean 2.
system.notes: Sire: MacNeil. Leads the Underground Society and the lone dissenter on the Prince's Council. Haven: several throughout the lower dock areas. Secrets rating: B+.

system.description:
Facetiously named, this power allows the Kindred to physically knock another character away from herself with the slightest of touches. Although this power does no damage in and of itself, its use is quite humbling — to be hurled away from an elder in a social setting has its embarrassing repercussions. Some Kindred use this power surreptitiously, touching their victims and sending them reeling across the room; others use it as a not-so-subtle display of their might, giving their victim a casual slap with overwhelming results.

System: The player spends a Blood Trait and must succeed in a physical challenge to touch the target (this may be done surreptitiously, but the player may not make use of other Potence benefits). The challenge is not required if the subject allows the player to touch him (a handshake, a “friendly” hand on the shoulder, etc). This power hurls the victim 20 feet directly away from the invoking character. If the subject strikes a wall or other solid obstacle, he suffers two health levels of bashing damage. Otherwise, the character needs to win a static physical challenge against six Traits to remain standing.

A Brujah with this power can stir the hearts of his allies, granting them courage and strength for the cause they fight for. Once employed, those affected fight fearlessly and with great strength, following the Cainite into battle against even overwhelming odds.

System: The player rolls Strength + Intimidation (difficulty 7). Any opposing power meant to inspire fear or otherwise prevent an affected ally from fighting suffers +2 difficulty. All affected allies — mortal, ghoul, or Cainite — also gain one dot of Potence for the scene per two successes. The number of successes determines how many allies are affected, from a single person (1 success) up to every ally in the vampire's immediate vicinity, such as a courtyard or battle group (5 successes).
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Three: Zealots

system.description: By spending a Blood Trait, you gain a further additional action at the end of the turn, on top of any gained from Swiftness.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description:
Assamites who hone both their preternatural senses and their speed learn a valuable secret: sometimes it is wiser to defend than to attack. A vampire with this power enters a brief trance in which she perceives every threat against her at once, assessing and reacting to each in turn.

System: At the start of a combat turn, before actions are declared, the player spends two Blood Traits and a Willpower Trait to activate this power (this counts as activating Celerity for the turn). The character takes no offensive action that turn, but may defend against every attack made against her, contesting each one individually. This power may be used no more than a number of times per scene equal to the character's Perception Trait total.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two: Saracens

system.description: By hissing and baring your vampiric features in a Social Challenge, you strike terror into a victim who, if defeated, flees and avoids you for the rest of the scene or hour, risking an extra Trait to act against you if cornered.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

vtmlarp.source: New Orleans by Night, Chapter Four: Characters
